headline: College Sports Commission Reports $355M in NIL Deals Cleared Since NIL Go Launch
summary: The CSC's latest data report shows 34,195 third-party NIL deals approved for a combined $355.24M since the NIL Go clearinghouse launched — still a fraction of the market's estimated $1B+ in annual third-party activity.

headline: CSC Raises Review Threshold for Smaller NIL Deals
summary: Deals between $600 and $15,000 will no longer face range-of-compensation review until an athlete's total associated deals cross $50,000 for the academic year — easing the compliance load for role players and smaller-market deals.

headline: On3 Retires Algorithm-Based NIL Valuation for a Deal-Based Model
summary: On3's NIL Valuation now tracks actual compensation athletes receive from schools and collectives rather than projected marketing value — a shift the outlet says better reflects real dollars moving through the market.

headline: Arch Manning Leads All College Athletes at $5.4M NIL Valuation
summary: The Texas quarterback heads into the 2026 season as the highest-valued NIL athlete in any sport, per On3's updated deal-based valuation model.

headline: Jeremiah Smith's NIL Portfolio Expands to Red Bull, Nintendo, EA Sports Cover
summary: The Ohio State receiver, valued at $4.2M, became the first college athlete to appear on a Red Bull can and holds a cover spot on EA Sports College Football 26 — placing him third among all college athletes in NIL value, behind only Manning and BYU's AJ Dybantsa.

headline: Big Ten Presidents Raise Alarm Over 'Associated Entities' Language in Protect College Sports Act
summary: Conference leadership warns that the federal bill's current wording on booster-funded 'associated entities' could strip hundreds of millions of dollars in NIL earnings from football and men's basketball players if left unaddressed.

headline: Tounde Yessoufou Withdraws From NBA Draft, Lands at St. John's
summary: The Baylor transfer and projected first-round pick pulled out of the draft to join Rick Pitino's program for 2026-27 — one of the highest-profile NIL-driven roster moves of the offseason.
